doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: How his father learned to write for big band
summary: Lessons from John Cotter, work with regional St. Louis-Kansas City bands, then Washington University for Stravinsky and Schoenberg.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Where did he learn his craft as far as just writing a big band arrangement? Was it just listening?

Well he actually said it was a guy named John Cotter who was — he was the musical director for Della Reese. And he learned a lot of the big band stuff there. And then he worked with a lot of the regional bands, Jeter-Pillars and a lot of the bands in the St. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

Louis-Kansas City area. There were several funeral directors, and I can’t remember some of the names of some of these guys, but they had big bands and Dad played there. So he learned how to write there. But in order to be able to write Stravinsky, Schoenberg, that kind of stuff, he went to school. And that’s when he went to study at Washington University.
